newsitem.title: UK: Budgens current sales up 7.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: Budgens current sales up 7.3 percent.

text.p: British supermarket group Budgens Plc said on Monday sales in the first eight weeks of the current year were up 7.3 percent as volumes rose 8.3 percent, offsetting lower product prices while higher margin fresh food sales rose.
Chief executive John von Spreckelsen added that operating profit margins had been maintained.

Budgens said pretax profits for the year ending April 27 jumped 19.7 percent to 9.07 million stg on turnover of 320.5 million, up from 302.8 million, and paid out a total dividend of 1.4 pence per share, up from 1.25 pence.
"We have achieved substantial growth in sales and profits despite fiercely competitive markets," von Spreckelsen said.
He added that there were plans to refurbish fourteen stores this year and to open ten new outlets.
Budgens said it had agreed with Kuwait Petroleum Corp to speed up the opening programme for Budgens stores on the company's petrol forecourts, starting early next year.
The company said that overall sales last year were up 7.2 percent as growth slowed in the second half due to a lack of inflation and "some attrition in November and December."
Budgens said same store sales in the year ending April 27 were up just one percent. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
